context:
Goal: know which review layers (reviewer, refuter, fix verifier, design reviewer) catch real defects, so a layer that only adds cost can go.
Problem (rule): the scorer is built and its fixture holds 10 past incidents, but a review record holds only a verdict per round, with no refuter field and no cost, so refuter and cost read unknown and reviewer recall can never read measured from real records; changing what a review record holds is your call.
Based on (read): the first review of the scoring work (its branch), 21:16 CST: 8 of the 10 incidents were reverted inside their own pull request before merge, and 6 are batch pull requests, which have no review record of their own (your ruling that a pull request carries its own review record).
Based on (read): the glossary says a finding is a reviewer's report; a verdict row is one PASS or FAIL per round.
Departs from: main — a review record holds a verdict and a head — b adds a refuter and a cost field to the record, c leaves the record alone.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped. The scoring tool is built and checked and goes on to be merged whichever you pick; only the later steps that measure real review records wait for your pick.

options.gain: No change to the review record; reviewer and fix-verifier recall become measurable from real records.
options.how: A later lane builds the verdicts file from review-record comments on merged pull requests; refuter and cost stay unknown in the report.
options.label: Read verdicts from the review-record comments as they are; leave refuter and cost unknown (recommended)
options.lose: The refuter and cost cells stay unknown until you change the record.

options.gain: All four layers and the cost are measured over time.
options.how: The record form gains two lines; the scorer reads them; every lane's record carries them from then on.
options.label: Add a refuter field and a cost field to every review record
options.lose: More text on every review, and a change to the merge tool that could hold merges while it lands.

options.gain: No unknown cells and no record change.
options.label: Score only the reviewer and the fix verifier; drop refuter and cost from the eval
options.lose: You never learn whether the refuter or the design reviewer earns its cost.

ref: owner chat 19:45 CST Nov 17 (relayed by the consultant): land the verification article's findings
reply: Closed on your pick a (14:36 CST): the scorer reads verdicts from the review-record comments as they are. On your question 'I have cost cells?': no. A review record today holds one verdict per round and a head; it has no cost and no refuter field (the first review of the scoring work, 21:16 CST Nov 17). So under a those two cells read unknown until you choose to add fields (option b), which you can still ask for later. Filed on step review-layer-recall-eval.
short: Review layers: where is a catch read from?

shown.label: Read verdicts from the review-record comments as they are; leave refuter and cost unknown (recommended)
Add a refuter field and a cost field to every review record
Score only the reviewer and the fix verifier; drop refuter and cost from the eval

title: To score what each review layer catches, where should the scorer read a catch from?
why: a measures what real records already hold at no change to the record form; b is the right second step once a shows a layer worth a field. Recommended by triage, not owner-typed.
